title: UGANDA: Uganda’s Kasese Diocese Marked Martyrs’ Day Virtually
desc:
By Masereka Peter
As Christians across Uganda marked the National Martyrs Day celebrations, the Bishop of Kasese Diocese, Rt. Rev. Francis Aquirinus Kibira Kambale called on believers to emulate the virtues of the Uganda Martyrs by standing firmly for truth, faithfulness, and self-sacrifice for the good of others.
The celebrations were held under a decentralized arrangement following the cancellation of the national event at Namugongo Martyrs Shrine due to the Ebola outbreak. The Mass was to be animated by Kasese Diocese.
In line with government health guidelines aimed at preventing the spread of the virus, the Uganda Episcopal Conference (UEC) directed that this year's commemorations be conducted at diocesan, parish, and local church levels under the guidance of respective Ordinaries.
While presiding over the Holy Mass virtually at Our Lady of Assumption Cathedral in Kasese Municipality, Bishop Kibira urged Christians to become modern-day martyrs through unwavering commitment to truth, fidelity, and service to humanity, emphasizing that genuine faith is demonstrated through sacrifice and concern for the welfare of others.
Bishop Kibira reminded Christians of this year’s theme, “Jesus Christ is Alive in You and Me,” and described Jesus Christ as the first and greatest martyr, who willingly sacrificed His life in obedience to His Father's mission of redeeming humanity from sin.
He urged believers to draw inspiration from Christ’s example by living lives characterized by faith, truth, and selfless service, noting that true discipleship requires commitment to God's will and a willingness to make sacrifices for the benefit of others.
The Vice Chairperson of the Steering Committee for the Uganda Martyrs Day celebrations at Namugongo, Mr. Joseph Nzukwa, expressed appreciation for the cooperation between the Government and the UEC in adopting a peaceful and responsible approach to the Martyrs Day celebrations amid concerns over the Ebola outbreak.
He said the decision demonstrated a shared commitment to safeguarding lives while ensuring that Christians continued to commemorate the faith and sacrifice of the Uganda Martyrs. Mr. Nzukwa also called on the faithful to continue contributing generously towards the construction and development of the cathedral, noting that their support was vital for the completion of ongoing church projects.
The Rwenzururu Prime Minister, Rt. Hon. Benson Baritazale Kule, called on various stakeholders to embrace the spirit of sacrifice and collective responsibility by contributing to the success and well-being of others.
He urged members of the public to emulate the selflessness of the Uganda Martyrs by putting the interests of their communities above personal gain.
In separate interviews outside, the Assistant RDC for Kasese District, Ms. Justine Muhindo, and the Chairperson of the Head of Laity at Our Lady of Assumption Cathedral Parish, Mrs. Asiimwe Tugume Queen Gonda, said all the prescribed Standard Operating Procedures had been strictly observed throughout the celebrations.
They noted that the measures put in place ensured the safety of the faithful while allowing them to participate in the commemorations. The two leaders expressed optimism that the virtual Martyrs Day celebrations would not only promote public health safety but also strengthen the faith and spiritual commitment of Christians.
In her emphasis, Ms Queen-Gonda said sustainable development and community progress can only be achieved when individuals, institutions, and leaders are willing to support one another and work towards common goals. END
